CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Intermittent tension-type headaches persisting for 2 weeks following occupational stress.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS (HPI):
35-year-old female presents with bilateral band-like tension headaches for 2 weeks. Mild photophobia, no nausea or focal deficits.
PRIOR CONSERVATIVE MANAGEMENT:
Trial of conservative treatment attempted with rest, hydration, and acetaminophen with partial relief.
PHYSICAL & NEUROLOGICAL EXAMINATION:
Vitals: BP 118/74, HR 68, SpO2 99% RA. Neurological examination normal: Cranial nerves II-XII intact, motor strength 5/5 globally,
reflexes 2+ symmetric, gait steady.
CLINICAL IMPRESSION & ASSESSMENT:
1. Acute tension-type headache.
2. No red flags or signs of intracranial pathology.
ORDER & CLINICAL RATIONALE:
CT Scan of Head with Contrast (CPT 70460) requested per patient preference. Contrast indicated per ordering note.
